description: UBOS, the statistics bureau of Uganda, publishes the final report of the 2024 National Population and Housing Census and a census profile report for each sub-region on its census page. Volume one, 434 pages, has a housing chapter on tenure, dwelling type, construction materials, drinking water, toilets and sanitation, waste disposal, lighting and cooking energy, and a chapter on solid waste and broken electrical equipment. The sub-region profiles go further down: district tables by county, subcounty and parish give drinking water and sanitation and the number of households using solar or electricity for lighting. Their indicator pages split lighting between grid and mini-grid electricity, solar home systems, solar lanterns, rechargeable torches, dry cells, candles and open fire; in Karamoja, for example, 2.2 percent of households used grid or mini-grid electricity and half used open fire. Coverage is national. Format and access: free PDF, no registration. Licence: a UBOS copyright and disclaimer page; no open licence was found. Caveats: parish tables are in long PDF reports and must be transcribed; the www host needed an extra intermediate certificate to verify. Simulation uses: parish-level solar and grid lighting shares for electrification planning, and water and sanitation access by subcounty. Related records: the WorldPop GRID3 census-based population grids.

schema_summary: Volume 1 chapter 11 housing: 11.1 tenure; 11.2 dwelling type; 11.3 construction materials; 11.5 drinking water source; 11.6 to 11.9 toilets, sanitation, handwashing, bathroom; 11.10 waste disposal; 11.11 lighting and cooking energy; 11.12 to 11.14 stoves, kitchens, cooking fuel; chapter 14 solid waste and non-functional electrical equipment; chapter 5 ICT and internet. Sub-region profiles: indicator pages (tenure, improved water, sanitation, cooking fuel, lighting by grid and mini-grid, solar home system, solar lantern, rechargeable torch, dry cell, candle, open fire) and district tables 1 to 15 by county, subcounty and parish, including Table 12 drinking water and sanitation and Table 13 households using solar or electricity for lighting.
